personal.name: Renée Walker
personal.title: Visual Designer
personal.overview: As a visual communication designer, researcher, and educator, I explore how design can deepen our understanding of the world through multisensory engagement, data-driven methods, and inclusive practices. My work bridges studio practice and scholarship, with ongoing research in information design, typography, and systems thinking across disciplines.

Faculty Appointments.title: Associate Professor, Visual Communication Design
Faculty Appointments.description:
Associate Professor and DEC Capstone Coordinator at Thomas Jefferson University. Teach and develop interdisciplinary courses in typography, information design, systems thinking, and human-centered design across undergraduate and graduate programs. Regularly partner with faculty and external organizations to lead student-centered initiatives addressing public health, harm reduction, and environmental storytelling.

Current research explores multisensory data visualization and embodied interaction, leveraging creative coding and participatory methodologies to engage users emotionally and physically. Projects include grant-funded installations, sensory workshops, and data-informed interfaces that visualize everything from bird song to emotional states. Faculty advisor for the AIGA Jefferson student chapter, mentoring emerging design leaders and supporting cross-institutional partnerships.

Faculty Appointments.title: Assistant Professor, Visual Communication Design
Faculty Appointments.description: Taught, coordinated and developed courses in typography, information design, systems thinking, and human-centered design spanning undergraduate and graduate programs. Fostered collaborative learning bridging design, engineering, and business. Faculty advisor for AIGA Jefferson student chapter.

Administrative Appointments.title: Capstone Coordinator, DEC Core
Administrative Appointments.description:
Bridge the Design, Engineering & Commerce schools by building systems that support collaborative, transdisciplinary learning. Work closely with capstone instructors across all three disciplines to align shared research methodologies, prototyping practices, and advising approaches — creating a more cohesive and connected experience for students navigating the capstone process.

Organize and host interdisciplinary panels, workshops, and networking events that bring students, faculty, and industry partners into dialogue across disciplinary boundaries. These gatherings surface unexpected connections, build cross-school community, and prepare students for collaborative professional practice. Develop shared resources — from research frameworks to process tools — that ensure the DEC curriculum functions as an integrated whole.

Professional / Industry Roles.title: Co-worker / Collaborator
Professional / Industry Roles.description: Member of shared workspace including graphic designers, type designers, industrial designers, architects and programmers. Participated in workshops, critiques, and lectures.

Professional / Industry Roles.title: Founding Partner & Creative Director
Professional / Industry Roles.description:
Founding principal of Gold Collective, a visual communication design studio specializing in identity systems, exhibition design, printed matter, and visual communication for social impact. Work with institutions, nonprofits, and cultural partners to develop storytelling strategies that translate complex data and systems into accessible, emotionally resonant experiences. Notable collaborators include Bard Music West, McSweeney's, RISD, SteegeThompson, and the University of Pennsylvania.

Recent studio work includes a university-wide campaign identity, NIH-funded visual tools for health risk communication, and the creative direction of multisensory exhibition experiences. Practice increasingly overlaps with grant-supported research — most recently through projects exploring participatory data interfaces and harm reduction pop-up spaces designed to engage Gen Z audiences.

Professional / Industry Roles.title: Graphic, Information & Environmental Designer
Professional / Industry Roles.description: Worked within interdisciplinary teams of architects, urban planners, marketing personnel, interior designers, and environmental graphics designers. Created and produced concepts for books, animations, handouts, and environmental graphics for architectural projects.

Professional / Industry Roles.title: Graphic & Editorial Designer
Professional / Industry Roles.description: Designed layouts for Pulitzer Prize winning weekly news publication. Coordinated and art directed photo shoots, created original artwork. Developed mapping system for Willamette Week's 2006 Finder magazine.

Professional / Industry Roles.title: Graphic & Editorial Designer
Professional / Industry Roles.description: Constructed editorial content and coordinated photography for Style, a weekly publication. Designed covers of special sections and various marketing material for in-house departments.

Teaching.title: Erasmus Professor | Wave Atelier: Prioritizing Laborers in a Tech-Driven World
Teaching.description: Co-taught an interdisciplinary architecture atelier exploring the future of work through the lens of Philadelphia's industrial history and evolving technological landscapes. Developed and led a sensory mapping assignment expanding traditional architectural research methods by incorporating multisensory and embodied data into the design process.
Teaching.citation: Walker, Renée "Prioritizing Laborers in a Tech-Driven World: A Philadelphia Perspective." Wave Atelier, Università IUAV di Venezia, Venice, Italy, Summer 2025.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Graphic Design II: Visual Narrative
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Explores how images and words work together to shape meaning and communicate across media. Students develop image-making skills through analog and digital workflows, emerging tools, and contemporary contexts. Positioned as the second course in the graphic design track and a direct expansion of Design II.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design VIII: Capstone in Graphic Design Communication
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Students independently develop and present a body of work demonstrating mastery of communication design theory, process, and principles, alongside a resume and curated portfolio. Guide and mentor students through project management, research, design development, and final presentation.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Experiential Graphic Design
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Introduces the field of Experiential Graphic Design (XGD) at the intersection of visual communication and the built environment, examining wayfinding, immersive learning environments, and branded spaces. Developed the course to engage students with real-world spaces and projects.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design VII: Systems Integration
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Students develop design concepts and establish a visual language applied across formats using a systems design approach, culminating in a written proposal for the following semester's Capstone project. Developed and co-developed projects examining formal, cultural, economic, and political systems and their impact on design.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design V: Introduction to Branding
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Focuses on the understanding and creation of cohesive identity systems, applying a systems approach to logo development, packaging, digital media, and related collateral. Coordinated community-engaged collaborations with nonprofit partners such as CDC Germantown United.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design II: Introduction to Graphic Design
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Introduction to the design process through the methods, materials, and vocabulary of graphic and web design, with emphasis on form analysis, visual design foundations, and image-making. Adapted and revised course content to include research activities and form exploration. Established a screenprinting studio for paper printing in collaboration with Surface Imaging.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design IV: Advanced Typography
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Builds on foundational typographic skills, with emphasis on the interplay of visual meaning, form, and typographic technicalities within a historical context. Co-developed projects, exercises, and lectures supporting technical, experimental, and culturally diverse learning outcomes.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Issues in Information Design
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Introduces the design and communication of information across categories including cartography, comparative data, and diagrams, with emphasis on exploration and process over finished craft. Refined existing course structure and developed projects that build core information design and communication skills.

Primary Teaching Responsibilities.title: Design III: Introduction to Typography
Primary Teaching Responsibilities.description: Introduces typography through sequential studies that build visual vocabulary, examining letterforms, text composition, and the grid with attention to hierarchy, legibility, and conceptual communication. Refreshed course content to foreground historical and technological forces that shaped typography, incorporating diverse cultural dialogue and hands-on letterform techniques.

Exhibitions.description: Energy Bodies is an interactive movement-capture installation that translates bodily expression into a dynamic, living visualization. Created by information designer, professor, and researcher Renée Walker and expressive arts therapist Carrie Powell, the project explores how inner sensations, emotions, and gestures can become data—revealing the energetic patterns that shape human experience.

Exhibitions.description: Utilizes the p5.js creative coding platform to visualize real-time thermoreceptive data from nine global cities. Grants Awarded.title: Pop-Up as Public Health: A Transdisciplinary Model for Urban Harm Reduction Education
Grants Awarded.institution: Smart and Healthy Cities, Thomas Jefferson University
Grants Awarded.description: Principal Investigator. Brings together students from Visual Communication Design, Sidney Kimmel Medical College, and Fashion Merchandising to design and stage a Harm Reduction-themed pop-up shop on Jefferson's East Falls campus. Leverages design as public health pedagogy and outreach targeting Gen Z learners, embedding harm reduction content in wearables, interactive materials, and QR-code-linked digital resources.

Grants Awarded.title: Mapping Creativity on the East Falls Campus
Grants Awarded.description: Co-Principal Investigator. Develop an interactive map of historical and contemporary creative achievement on the East Falls campus through student-led data gathering, systemic cataloging, and design prototyping across cartography, comparative data, and diagram formats.

Grants Awarded.title: Data Sense: Computation Methods for Information Display
Grants Awarded.description: Principal Investigator. Explore computation methods for information display by experimenting with p5.js and JSON data to generate multisensory visualizations of day-to-day information. Investigates whether design-friendly coding platforms can make information visualization more intuitive and accessible through a multisensory approach to cognitive perception.

Grants Awarded.title: Blurring Boundaries Design Studio: Food & Culture Experience
Grants Awarded.institution: CFDNL Pedagogy Grant, Thomas Jefferson University
Grants Awarded.description: Co-Principal Investigator (33%). Engage Visual Communication Design and Interior Design students in an interdisciplinary studio learning environment centered on non-western street food restaurant design—working with real Philadelphia-based food truck clients on 2D logos, menus, environmental graphics, and spatial concepts. Advance diversity, equity, and inclusion through collaborative cross-disciplinary practice.
